skill.name: published-vs-planned
skill.description: Load whenever an agent has scheduled, uploaded or published content (posts, reels, stories, videos, files) on a social scheduler or a drive and must say what is actually live. Use it for "check what was actually published", "did it post", "is it scheduled", "nothing is published", "did the upload save", "revisa lo publicado", "¿ya salió?", "no salió en Instagram", "programado", "¿ya se guardó todo?", "nada está en el Drive". It builds a plan list, reads each item back from the scheduler's own list, and after the slot passes checks the LIVE public page, then reports only a planned / scheduled / live table. It never says "published", "scheduled" or "done" because a tool said success. Works for Meta Business Suite, TikTok, LinkedIn, Buffer, any scheduler, and for files uploaded to a drive. Not for designing posts or writing captions, and not for ad performance or reach numbers.
skill.summary: Compare approved plans with scheduler entries, live posts, and uploaded files using timestamped verification tables.
skill.author: rabbitdesigns22

content.user_title: Verify Published Content Against Your Plan
content.value_statement: Scheduler confirmations do not prove that posts are live or uploads are accessible. This skill guides evidence-based checks against approved plans and produces timestamped reconciliation tables.
actual_capabilities: Build one planned row per item and network, including account, format, timezone, asset, and caption details.
Compare planned items with scheduler list entries, checking timing, media previews, caption integrity, and destination accounts.
Verify live posts after their planned times, checking each network separately and accounting for format-specific locations.
Check uploaded files in destination folders for correct names, nonzero sizes, and successful opening.
Report gaps first with explicit verification statuses, check timestamps, likely causes, and proposed fixes.
Compare recurring checks with the previous timestamped table and report changed rows.
limitations: This is a workflow guide, not a bundled scheduler integration; actual checks depend on available tools and authorized access.
Private or restricted accounts cannot be verified without access, and platform lists may update with a delay.
Recurring checks require an existing execution arrangement; the skill does not provide its own background scheduler.
Checks establish content existence and fidelity, not reach, impressions, advertising performance, or audience engagement.

use_cases.title: Reconcile client publishing
use_cases.description: Compare approved client calendars with scheduler queues and live profiles, separating Facebook and Instagram results.

use_cases.title: Confirm campaign launch posts
use_cases.description: Check launch assets, captions, accounts, and timing after scheduled slots, then report missing or incorrect items.

use_cases.title: Verify shared file deliveries
use_cases.description: Confirm expected files appear in destination folders, have nonzero sizes, and open successfully before reporting delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Check a single post
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether [post] is live on [account]. Use [planned time and timezone]. Report the evidence and check time; mark unavailable access as not checked.

prompt_templates.title: Reconcile an approved calendar
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [approved calendar] with [scheduler] entries. Check each account, network, format, timezone, asset, and caption. Return the reconciliation table with gaps first.

prompt_templates.title: Audit live posts and delivered files
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [campaign plan] across [networks] and [destination folder]. Verify due posts and uploaded files. Mark future slots not yet due. Request approval before changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: reconcile posts and file deliveries.

prompt_templates.title: Compare recurring verification results
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [previous timestamped table] with current evidence for [plan]. Report changed rows, unresolved gaps, and the current timezone. Request approval before corrective actions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review changes between recurring checks.

output_examples.input: Illustrative check: two cross-posted items were planned for 10:00 UTC. Both scheduler entries exist, but only Facebook is live.
output: Checked 4 November, 10:10 UTC: one of two items verified live.
Instagram reel: planned 10:00 UTC; scheduled ok; live missing. Likely cause: cross-post failure. Fix: request approval to republish, then verify.
Facebook post: planned 10:00 UTC; scheduled ok; live ok. No gap found.

output_examples.input: Illustrative delivery check: launch.pdf opens in the destination folder, but budget.xlsx cannot be checked because access expired.
output: Checked 4 November, 15:00 UTC: one file verified; one file not checked.
budget.xlsx: destination not checked because access expired. Fix: restore authorized access and repeat verification.
launch.pdf: correct destination and filename; size greater than zero; opens successfully.

best_practices: Start from the approved calendar and record a timezone for every planned item.
Verify scheduler entries independently from live posts, and check each network separately.
Timestamp each report, retain the previous table, and obtain required approval before corrective actions.
anti_patterns: Calling an item published solely because a tool, toast, log, or earlier report says it succeeded.
Treating a successful cross-post on one network as proof that all destinations are live.
Marking inaccessible, delayed, expired, or incorrectly filtered content as missing without checking the relevant context.

faq.question: Does this skill publish posts automatically?
faq.answer: Its primary purpose is verification. It describes corrective actions, but execution requires available tools, authorized access, and owner approval where required.

faq.question: Which scheduling platforms does it cover?
faq.answer: The workflow applies to Meta Business Suite, TikTok, LinkedIn, Buffer, and other schedulers. It does not bundle platform connectors.

faq.question: Can it verify private accounts?
faq.answer: Only with authorized access. Otherwise, it reports not checked and explains the access limitation.

faq.question: How are timezone differences handled?
faq.answer: Each planned row includes a timezone. Scheduler entries are compared against that plan to identify timing mismatches.

faq.question: Can it verify uploaded files?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides checks of destination folders, filenames, nonzero file sizes, and whether files open successfully.

faq.question: Does it measure engagement or run background checks?
faq.answer: No. It verifies existence and fidelity, not engagement. Recurring execution requires an existing automation or a separate check.
